strategies.name: Detect Persistence via Outlook Home Page Exploitation

analytics.name: Analytic 0502
analytics.guidance: Adversary uses a tool like Ruler to configure a malicious Outlook folder Home Page that loads a remote or embedded HTML payload upon folder interaction. Execution chain begins with Outlook launching, a specific folder being accessed, and a suspicious child process being spawned or COM-based execution invoked.

tuning.description: Home Page can be configured on any folder like Calendar, Inbox, or custom folders
The Home Page URL may point to internal or external content, hosted on trusted or unknown domains
Execution may result in launch of scripting hosts (e.g., mshta.exe, wscript.exe) from outlook.exe
Execution may occur only when the specific folder is accessed after launch, not immediately at startup
Behavior may vary if the folder's form view is customized or suppressed via GPO

log_sources.name: WinEventLog:Application
log_sources.channel: Outlook logs indicating failure to load or render HTML page in Home Page view

log_sources.name: WinEventLog:PowerShell
log_sources.channel: Execution of PowerShell script to enumerate or remove malicious Home Page folder config

analytics.name: Analytic 0503
analytics.guidance: Malicious HTML or script is rendered as a Home Page for a specific Outlook folder. Outlook accesses that folder, loads remote content, and executes embedded JavaScript or ActiveX/COM logic resulting in unauthorized actions or local execution.

tuning.description: Home Page customization may not be audited unless detailed message or folder auditing is enabled
Anomalous access to folders not usually interacted with can signal triggering of malicious view
Mail clients may restrict remote Home Page content unless domain is explicitly allowed

log_sources.name: m365:unified
log_sources.channel: Folder configuration updated with external or HTML-formatted Home Page via Set-MailboxFolder

log_sources.name: m365:messagetrace
log_sources.channel: Inbound email triggering Outlook to auto-access folder tied to malicious Home Page
